events.title: Swiss Market Ends Higher For 5th Straight Session
events.description:
Swiss stocks moved higher on Thursday, extending gains to a fifth straight session, thanks to strong buying at several counters. In addition to digesting Swiss producer and import prices data, investors looked ahead to corporate earnings updates.

The benchmark SMI settled with a gain of 219.58 points or 1.55% at 14,349.51, the day's high.

events.title: Major European Markets Close On Firm Note
events.description: The major European markets closed higher on Thursday, supported by gains in retail, luxury, pharmaceuticals and industrials sectors even as tech stocks were under some pressure amid uncertainty about returns on AI-related investments. Softening global bond yields and strong UK GDP data aided sentiment.

events.title: U.S. Business Inventories Increase In Line With Estimates In August
events.description: Business inventories in the U.S. increased in line with economist estimates in the month of August, according to a report released by the Commerce Department on Thursday. The Commerce Department said business inventories rose by 0.4 percent in August after climbing by an upwardly revised 0.9 percent in July.

events.title: New York Manufacturing Index Surges To Nearly Five-Year High In October
events.description: New York manufacturing activity rose sharply in the month of October, according to a report released by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Thursday. The New York Fed said its general business conditions index surged to 25.5 in October from 7.6 in September, with a positive reading indicating growth. Economists had expected the index to rise to 10.3.

events.title: Philly Fed Index Tumbles In October But Still Indicates Growth
events.description: A report released by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia on Thursday showed a steep drop by its reading on regional manufacturing activity in the month of October. The Philly Fed said its diffusion index for current general activity plunged to 20.9 in October from 37.8 in September, although a positive reading still indicates growth. Economists had expected the index to drop to 30.0.

events.title: U.S. Retail Sales Climb More Than Expected Amid Higher Gas Prices
events.description: The Commerce Department released a report on Thursday showing retail sales in the U.S. increased by much more than expected in in the month of September. The report said retail sales climbed by 0.8 percent in September after surging by an upwardly revised 1.3 percent in August. Economists had expected retail sales to rise by 0.3 percent.

events.title: U.S. Producer Prices Jump 1.3% In September, Much More Than Expected
events.description: Following yesterday's report on consumer price inflation, the Labor Department released a separate report on Thursday showing producer prices in the U.S. shot up by much more than expected in the month of September. The Labor Department said its producer price index for final demand jumped by 1.3 in September after rising by an upwardly revised 0.5 percent in August.

events.title: U.S. Weekly Jobless Claims Inch Up Slightly Less Than Expected
events.description: A report released by the Labor Department on Thursday showed first-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits edged slightly higher in the week ended October 10th. The Labor Department said initial jobless claims ticked up to 199,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level of 198,000. Economists had expected jobless claims to rise to 200,000.

events.title: Bay Street May Open Higher, But Tech Weakness May Weigh
events.description: The Canadian market may open higher on Thursday, tracking firm precious metals and oil prices. However, a sell-off in global tech stocks amid concerns over returns on AI-related investments could hurt sentiment and limit market's upside.

events.title: Growth Surprise Lifts FTSE 100
events.description: The FTSE 100 benchmark of the London Stock Exchange rallied on Thursday amidst positive sentiment generated by the better-than-expected GDP reading.
